Evelyn — I ran a quick pass on the telemetry and have a few notes / assumptions for the sizing draft:

- Baseline model: assume Llama2-13B quantized to 4-bit (FP16-equivalent perf via kernel optimizations); if Nimbus insists on a different model we will re-run the perf matrix.
- Memory: streaming sessions increase KV cache pressure; for the observed mix (30% streaming) plan for +25% GPU memory headroom per node.
- Concurrency: treat the 650 spike as a short fan-out — for autoscaling planning, allocate capacity for sustaining 200 concurrent active sessions with headroom for 650 as transient burst via queued capacity + autoscale ramp.
- Latency: for the Q/A path (avg ~600 token total) targeting P95 <= 400ms implies using batching window <= 10ms and ~8-12 tokens/ms throughput on chosen GPU.

Proposal (first-pass):
- Dedicated pool: 6x A100-80GB equiv nodes (or 8x GA100v2 64GB) with auto-burst pool of 3 extra nodes.
- Software: quantization to 4-bit with Redwood's KV caching enabled and continuous batching.
- Fallbacks: add a cheaper 4x V100-style backup for low-cost overflow if high-cost capacity is saturated (keeps overall unit economics bounded).

Open q's for Nimbus: exact P95 targets per endpoint (Maria to confirm), and whether any flows require persistent session pinning (stateful session affinity) — that impacts routing and node reservation.

I can inline these assumptions into the sizing draft. Evelyn, let me know if you want different wording for customers.

-Ben

Hi Maria — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarifications. Attached is a short draft (dedicated-sizing-draft.pdf) that captures Ben's assumptions and a recommended initial pool so your infra team can review. Highlights:

- Initial pool: 6 high-memory GPUs + 3-burst nodes to cover short spikes; autoscaling policy tuned for 60s ramp for non-critical flows.
- Performance knobs: 4-bit quantization, KV-prefix caching for common prompts, batching window <=10ms for Q/A endpoints.
- Ops: we recommend session-level instrumentation and a low-latency circuit-breaker for the long-summary flow to protect Q/A SLAs.

Next steps:
1) Maria: confirm per-endpoint P95 targets and whether any endpoints need session pinning (you offered to pull endpoint names and slices).
2) Nimbus infra: can your security team confirm acceptability of 4-bit quantization (we will provide the audit notes and KMS integration checklist).
3) Redwood: we'll convert the draft into a Zone/Pool template for the Dedicated UI and surface estimated monthly cost.

If the Nimbus team is happy with the approach, we can schedule a short 45-min review with Ben and Marissa next week to finalize SKUs and rollout timeline.
